newsitem.title: USA: U.S. troops prepare for deployment to Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops prepare for deployment to Gulf.

text.p: Army troops based at Fort Hood, Texas, made final preparations on Saturday for deployment to the Gulf and possible military strikes against Iraq.
The Pentagon on Friday said the United States would send 5,000 additional Army troops to Kuwait. Defense officials at Fort Hood said the actual deployment from there would be about 3,000.
"They are in the preparation stage, getting ready to go. They're waiting for the word," said Staff Sgt. Monica McNeal, adding the official deployment order would probably come down on Sunday.
She said the preparations included soldiers pulling together their belongings, talking to their families and perhaps changing their insurance policies or making out wills.

McNeal said members of two battalions and a Brigade Combat Team headquarters, as well as backup maintenance and medical staff, would be deployed under Exercise Intrinsic Action, a program begun last year to train Kuwaiti soldiers.
She said tanks and other equipment were already in place in Kuwait so the troops would travel only with individual gear.
The soldiers were to join 1,200 others already in Kuwait and would become the latest addition to a U.S. military buildup of planes, warships and ground forces.

Eight radar-dodging Stealth warplanes arrived in Kuwait on Friday. Four U.S. B-52 bombers with cruise missiles rebased to the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia, and the aircraft carrier Enterprise was also en route to the Gulf with some 75 warplanes to join the carrier Carl Vinson, already on patrol there.
